deep_status: Read where your session stands: the hub's gates, and each of your claims with its runs, its verdict and any run that contradicts what you predicted. Its result does not prove your work is done: only a verdict the checks reached says so, and a claim with no verdict is still open. Verdict, never: Written by an agent or an extension, or a PASS resting on a model's judgment alone: each assertion names its oracle, code, model or person. Task definition of done, never: Drafted from the working session's work, or changed by it.
deep_search: Search your wiki, past decisions and the project's spec, and in your own session its open items and verdicts, read only; every hit names its source. A hit does not prove what it quotes still holds: it is what its source said, read through an index that is never the source of truth. Event, never: Written under another writer's name, changed or deleted. Index, never: The source of truth; the wiki's pages are. Source and reading, never: Called from a panel or past its quota, or a reading without its source and as-of time, or a tool not counted as read.
deep_ask: Ask the person what only they can answer, a taste call or a choice, or raise a task only a person can do, naming the check that will prove it done. It waits for the answer and returns it, or says it is still waiting, with the ask's deadline and default. An answer does not prove anything about your work, and a task answered as done does not prove it is: only its check passing does. Ask, never: Answered by an agent, or by an extension except by naming a decision, rule, budget or request of yours that the core checks.
deep_wait: Keep waiting on an ask you raised, once deep_ask says it is still waiting. Still waiting does not prove the ask was seen; its default applies at its deadline. Ask, never: Answered by an agent, or by an extension except by naming a decision, rule, budget or request of yours that the core checks.
deep_open_item: Record what is still open on your task, such as a kind or a field a piece needs that does not exist, instead of working around it. Recording an open item does not prove it matters, and you can't close your own without evidence. Evidence and open item, never: An open item closed by its own agent without evidence.
deep_claim: Declare your task done at a commit, with what you expect each check to show before it runs; the checks then decide. A claim does not prove the task is done: the verdict comes from the checks' runs, and a run that disagrees with your prediction shows as a contradiction. Claim, never: Given a verdict by its own agent.
deep_evidence: Attach a file from your working folder as evidence, stored by its hash. Storing a file does not prove what it shows; a path outside your working folder is answered as one that doesn't exist. Evidence and open item, never: An open item closed by its own agent without evidence.
deep_run: Run a check the repo's spec names, for your claim at its commit; it answers with the run's outcome and its evidence once the run finishes. One run's outcome does not prove your claim passes: only a verdict over the runs a claim needs says so. Check, never: Edited once protected, or the only cover for a claim when that claim's agent wrote it.
